topic: Getting in and out of the car all day: back care for drivers

slides.headline: In and out of the car all day?
slides.sub: Couriers, tradies and reps: small habits that make a long driving day easier.

slides.title: Sit first, then swing
slides.body: Getting in, sit on the seat with your feet still outside, then turn your knees and legs in together. Reverse it to get out. It spares your back the twist-and-duck.

slides.title: Set the seat up once
slides.body: Seat close enough to reach the pedals with a slight knee bend, backrest fairly upright rather than reclined, and a small lumbar support if it feels better. Worth checking in any new vehicle.

slides.title: Use every stop
slides.body: Each time you get out, take ten seconds: stand tall, lean back gently, walk a few steps. Short, frequent movement breaks add up over a long day behind the wheel.

slides.title: Lifting from the boot
slides.body: Slide the load close to the edge of the boot before lifting, keep it near your body and use your legs. A crate or step to raise heavy items can make a big difference.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Back pain with numbness in the legs or saddle area, new bladder or bowel changes, or pain that keeps getting worse despite rest deserve prompt medical attention.

slides.headline: Driving all day for work?
slides.body: Our chiropractors at Hybrid Physiotherapy assess your back and daily routine, and combine hands-on care with practical exercises. Book online, link in bio.

caption:
Forty stops a day and your back feels every single one?

For couriers, tradies and sales reps, it's often the getting in and out rather than the driving itself. Try sitting first with your feet outside, then swinging your legs in together. Set your seat up once so you're not reaching for the pedals, and use each stop for ten seconds of standing tall and a few steps.

When lifting from the boot, slide the load close first and use your legs.

Numbness in the legs or saddle area, or bladder changes, need prompt medical attention.

story.headline: Driving for work?
story.body: Sit first, then swing both legs in together. Reverse it to get out. Your back will notice.
